requirement: Describe NI071F2 as a Phase 3, randomized, double-blind, multicenter, three-stage study comparing NI-071 with US-licensed Remicade in rheumatoid arthritis, with Stage 1 biosimilarity, Stage 2 interchangeability, and Stage 3 long-term safety follow-up.

evidence.text: Protocol Version 4 synopsis defines the three-stage design.
SAP Version 5 restates the design.

requirement: Initially randomize participants 2:1 to Remicade-US or NI-071, stratified by baseline CRP at 2 mg/dL or less versus above 2 mg/dL; at Week 22 re-randomize eligible Remicade-US participants 1:1 to continue Remicade-US or enter the alternating Switch sequence.

evidence.text: The protocol defines both randomizations and stratification.
The SAP confirms treatment sequences.

requirement: Define the Stage-1 primary endpoint as ACR20 response using CRP at Week 22, with response requiring at least 20% improvement in tender and swollen joint counts plus at least 20% improvement in three of the five remaining ACR core-set measures.

evidence.text: The protocol defines the primary biosimilarity endpoint.
The SAP specifies the ACR20 derivation.

requirement: Use all randomized participants analyzed according to Stage-1 assignment as the ITT population for the primary biosimilarity analysis.

evidence.text: The SAP defines ITT and its primary use.

requirement: Define safety as all participants receiving study drug and group them according to treatment received within each stage.

evidence.text: The SAP defines the safety population and attribution.

requirement: Use a blinded-review-defined per-protocol Stage-1 population with a Week-22 ACR20-CRP assessment and no major deviations affecting the primary endpoint for sensitivity, and a distinct Stage-2 PK per-protocol population completing required switch treatments for interchangeability.

evidence.text: The SAP defines stage-specific PP populations.

requirement: Estimate the Week-22 ACR20-CRP response-rate difference for NI-071 minus Remicade-US and apply two one-sided Wald tests; conclude efficacy biosimilarity only if both null hypotheses are rejected using asymmetric equivalence margins of -12% and +15%.

evidence.text: The SAP specifies the TOST analysis and asymmetric margins.

requirement: For the primary Week-22 analysis, classify missing ACR20-CRP, dropout, and discontinuation of study drug on or before Week 14 as nonresponse; do not use LOCF mixed components for the primary endpoint.
acceptable_values: no LOCF mixed components for primary

evidence.text: The SAP defines primary composite nonresponse rules.

requirement: Justify Stage-1 enrollment using expected ACR20 response rates, the asymmetric -12%/+15% equivalence margins, 2:1 allocation, two one-sided 2.5% tests, desired power, and allowance for missing primary outcomes; separately justify the Stage-2 interchangeability PK sample.

evidence.text: The protocol gives efficacy and PK sample-size assumptions.
The SAP documents final sample-size calculations.

requirement: Treat Stage-2 PK interchangeability as confirmatory only if Stage-1 efficacy biosimilarity succeeds; otherwise report interchangeability analyses as descriptive or supportive and avoid formal claims.

evidence.text: The SAP specifies the confirmatory gate between stages.

requirement: Repeat primary biosimilarity analyses in FAS and PP populations; assess LOCF mixed-component ACR20, covariate-adjusted logistic models, geographic and disease-status effects, and a tipping-point analysis that varies response among participants with missing Week-22 data.

evidence.text: The SAP enumerates five primary sensitivity strategies.

requirement: Analyze secondary efficacy endpoints including ACR20 at other visits, ACR50/70, DAS28-CRP/ESR, RAPID3, HAQ-DI, SF-36, and individual ACR core measures by stage and treatment without promoting them to the primary biosimilarity claim.

evidence.text: The protocol lists secondary efficacy endpoints.
The SAP specifies secondary analyses.

requirement: Apply prespecified component-level rules for ACR20/50/70, DAS28, HAQ-DI, SF-36, tender and swollen joint counts, and visual-analog scales, clearly distinguishing calculable partial questionnaires from endpoints that remain missing.

evidence.text: The SAP provides endpoint derivation and component missingness rules.

requirement: For Stage-2 interchangeability, analyze prespecified steady-state PK exposure parameters in the Stage-2 PK per-protocol population using log-transformed measures and 90% confidence intervals for geometric-mean ratios against the prespecified equivalence limits.

evidence.text: The protocol defines the interchangeability PK objective.
The SAP specifies the PK equivalence analysis.

requirement: Summarize stage-emergent and overall treatment-emergent adverse events by MedDRA SOC/PT, severity, relationship, seriousness, discontinuation, death, infections, infusion reactions, and other events of special interest; conservatively impute missing relationship, severity, and seriousness as related, severe, and serious for summaries.

evidence.text: The protocol defines safety endpoints.
The SAP specifies event summaries and conservative missing conventions.

requirement: Document that SAP Version 5 updates the per-protocol definition to exclude only major deviations affecting the primary endpoint and confirm this change was finalized through blinded data review before unblinding.

evidence.text: The SAP records the change from the protocol and timing of blinded review.

requirement: Confirm the SAP-only asymmetric-margin Wald implementation, primary composite nonresponse rule, Stage-2 PK equivalence parameters and limits, PP definitions, and tipping-point algorithm before making them binding in a protocol-only plan.

evidence.text: The protocol delegates operational statistical details.
The SAP contains later operational decisions.

notes: These choices must be surfaced as confirmed decisions rather than guessed from the protocol.
